name: Rice-paper & cheese bake — logged batch (cottage + 9% + cheddar)

source.author: Logged batch — actually cooked 2026-09-25
source.notes: A batch the user actually cooked, logged as a reference. Distinct cheese blend from the base rice_paper_cheese_bake (this one is cottage-forward + cheddar). TOTAL batch = 3 rice-paper sheets (~33 g) + 250 g cottage cheese + 130 g combined cheese (75 g of 9% light yellow + 55 g cheddar at 28% fat, 3 slices). Makes 2 units; macros below are PER UNIT (batch ÷ 2). ASSUMPTIONS (not given): ~½ of one beaten egg actually sticking as the wash + ~3 g sesame, and NO added salt — tell me if you salted it or used more/less egg and I'll adjust. Estimate.

serving_desc: 1 unit (~200 g cooked) — the batch makes 2

ingredients.note: tell me if you salted it

steps: Mix the cottage, 9% yellow and cheddar; season with pepper.
On parchment layer: rice paper → half the cheese → rice paper → rest of cheese → rice paper on top.
Brush both sides with beaten egg, sprinkle sesame.
Bake at 200 °C for 25–30 min until golden and crispy; cut into 2 units.

batch_totals.note: Whole batch (2 units), incl. assumed ~½ egg wash + ~3 g sesame. Cheeses drive the fat, saturated fat and sodium; the cheddar (28% fat) is the richest lever.

him.verdict: Excellent protein density for what it is — ~32 g protein per unit for only 387 kcal is ~8.3 g protein per 100 kcal, one of the best snacks in your library. The cottage-forward blend is what does it: 250 g of cottage keeps protein high while the fat stays moderate for a cheese bake (~19 g/unit, ~11 g saturated), and the cheddar is the richest lever. Downsides are the usual for this dish: barely any fiber (~0.4 g) and high sodium (~800 mg/unit even with no added salt). A genuinely strong high-protein snack — just pair it with something fibrous.
flags: ~32 g protein / unit at 387 kcal — ~8.3 g protein per 100 kcal (excellent)
moderate fat ~19 g/unit (~11 g saturated) — cheddar is the richest lever
very low fiber (~0.4 g) — no veg, refined rice-paper carbs
high sodium (~800 mg/unit) from the cheeses alone — good you skipped added salt
suggested_mods: Keep it: swapping some cheddar for more 9% cheese would trim fat with little protein cost
Serve with salad / tomato / pepper for the fiber + vitamin C it lacks
Great post-workout or as the protein anchor of a lighter day

her_preconception.verdict: A high-protein, calcium-rich dairy snack, fully baked (egg wash cooked through). Cottage, 9% yellow and cheddar are all pasteurized hard/fresh cheeses — no Listeria concern, and no Bulgarian/soft cheese in this batch, so no safety flag at all. Strong calcium and protein for her; not a folate/iron/DHA source, so it's a snack rather than a prenatal main.
prenatal_highlights: some choline from the egg wash
fully baked, all pasteurized cheeses — no safety flags
suggested_mods: Pair with salad/tomato for folate + vitamin C
Fine as-is; no swaps needed for safety this time

cooking_guide: Mix the cottage, 9% yellow and cheddar with pepper until fairly even. This blend is cottage-forward, so it's a bit wetter — that's fine, it helps the rice paper soften and seal.
Keep the rice papers DRY (don't soak). Line a tray with parchment.
Layer: one rice paper → half the cheese (leave a ~1 cm border) → second rice paper → rest of the cheese → third rice paper on top. Press gently all over to seal.
Brush the top with beaten egg (this is what gives the deep-golden, shatter-crisp surface), scatter sesame, then carefully flip and brush + sesame the other side too.
Bake in a fully preheated oven at 200 °C (400 °F) for 25–30 min. The cheddar makes it a little greasier/crispier — if it's browning unevenly, flip once around 15 min.
Pull it deep golden and crackly; rice paper burns fast, so watch the last 5 min.
Rest 2–3 min on a rack so it crisps as it cools, then cut into 2 units with a serrated knife.
Tip: since you skipped salt, a pinch of za'atar or dried oregano in the cheese adds savoriness without much sodium; a spoon of cooked spinach folded in adds the fiber this bake lacks.
